info.description:
Server-to-server API that LavBench uses to run competition workspaces on nano-colab.

## Authentication
Every call except the signed storage links sends `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`. Keys look like
`ncak_<key id>_<secret>`, are issued per client and live only in the LavBench backend. nano-colab stores
only their SHA-256. Each operation lists the scope it needs in `x-required-scope`. A missing or unknown key
gets 401; a key without the scope gets 403. Browsers never call this API.

## Typical flow
1. `GET /v1/images` to choose an `image_id`.
2. Upload the task package: `POST /v1/assets/{version}/uploads`, PUT the ZIP to the returned URL,
   `POST /v1/assets/{version}/complete`, then poll `GET /v1/assets/{version}` until `READY`.
3. `PUT /v1/events/{external_id}` with the stage's schedule and profile. Repeat it with `published: true` to
   publish, and repeat it again whenever LavBench changes the stage. LavBench timing is the source of truth.
4. Poll `GET /v1/events/{external_id}/readiness` until `READY`.
5. When a competitor opens their environment: `PUT /v1/events/{external_id}/workspaces/{external_user_id}`,
   then `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/launch`, and hand the token to that competitor's browser.
6. To collect submissions: `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/export/raw` streams one declared file
   (`.../export/metadata` gives its size and SHA-256 without content); `.../export` returns small files
   as base64 JSON.
7. `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/stop` stops a competitor's notebook server and keeps the disk.
   `POST /v1/events/{external_id}/cancel` stops every server of an event and blocks new launches;
   `GET /v1/events` lists the client's own events, for finding events to cancel.

## Conventions
- IDs are deterministic. Every PUT is an idempotent upsert, so a timed-out request can be repeated as-is.
- Times are ISO 8601 and must include a timezone.
- Errors return `{"detail": ...}`. 409 and 503 responses may carry `Retry-After` (seconds); wait at least
  that long before retrying. Other 4xx errors will not succeed on retry.
- Launch tokens, upload URLs and exported file contents are secrets or student data: do not log them.

put.description: Idempotent upsert keyed by the client's own event ID. Returns 201 when the event is created and 200 otherwise; repeating the same request is safe. Drafts can change freely. Setting published=true publishes the event, which cannot be undone. After that only name, export_paths and a later end time may change, and moving the end records an extension. Publishing or extending an event can be refused when it would exceed approved capacity.

403.description: The API key lacks the events:write scope

409.description: Conflicting change: a frozen field changed after publication, an attempt to unpublish, a capacity refusal, a task package owned by another client, or a cancelled event

post.description: Marks the event cancelled, which cannot be undone: no new workspaces, launch tokens or launches, later PUTs are refused, and readiness reports BLOCKED. Then stops every notebook server that runs one of its workspaces and keeps their disks; they are archived and purged on the event's normal schedule. Idempotent: repeat the call until it returns 200 to retry servers that did not stop.

404.description: No event with this ID belongs to the client

503.description: The event is cancelled but some servers could not be stopped yet; repeat the call

post.description: Returns the requested files from the running workspace (LIVE) or, after the event, from the verified archive (ARCHIVE). A LIVE read happens only while the account's notebook server runs this workspace, never from another event's workspace. Only paths declared in the event's export_paths can be read. Each file has its SHA-256 and every export is audited. Files over the size limit come back as TOO_LARGE without content. Prefer POST .../export/raw, which streams one file.

post.description: Streams one declared file as application/octet-stream, from the running workspace (LIVE) or, after the event, from the verified archive (ARCHIVE), under the same rules as POST .../export. Content-Length and Repr-Digest (RFC 9530, sha-256) are sent before the body; the bytes are checked against both while streaming, and a file that changes mid-read ends the response early, so a body shorter than Content-Length or with another SHA-256 must be discarded. Every export is audited.
